title: ARIA production-autonomous enterprise mode had prose intent without live SSOT enforcement for policy owners, required merge checks, rollback proof, incident proof, runner attestation, and token/DLP hard-fail evidence
resolved_by: Enterprise SSOT owner modules and merge_authority fail-closed enforcement

missing_live_owners: Risk policy classification had no schema-bound policy owner producing policy hash and reason codes.
Autonomy unlock thresholds were prose goals rather than ledger-replayed counters.
L3 approval did not require two-stage human approval bound to PR, head SHA, policy hash, expiry, and separation of duties.
Rollback bundle, rollback simulation, runner attestation, and incident rows were not hard gates for autonomous merge.
missing_merge_authority_enforcement: aria-merge-authority was not a live required PR status check.
Branch protection proof did not require exact required checks, signed commits, reviews, conversation resolution, ruleset IDs, bypass actor absence, force-push disablement, and delete disablement.
Token proof did not structurally forbid GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, or PAT mutation-token fallback for autonomous merge.
DLP proof did not require scanner output across diff, prompt, transcript, logs, and artifacts.
evidence.regression_risk: A failed adapter.merge_pr path could write a merged lifecycle event unless merge_authority owned success-only lifecycle emission.

structural_root_cause.summary: The system had strong ARIA runtime primitives but no single executable policy-owner chain feeding merge_authority as the only autonomous merge boundary.
structural_root_cause.ssot_gap: Capabilities were described across docs and readiness claims, but each enterprise capability lacked one canonical owner module, declared state surface, schema-bound policy input, and required check integration.
structural_root_cause.required_property: Autonomous production merge must be impossible unless every owner module can replay ledger evidence and merge_authority observes the final live PR/head state immediately before merge.

merge_gate_order: incident finalization and success-only lifecycle event
